name: Cocaine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Increases extracellular DA/NE/5-HT by transporter blockade; stabilises DAT in outward-facing open conformation (fast binding/dissociation). Striatal DA spike drives D1/D2 signalling responsible for reinforcement.

neuroimaging.finding: 60-77% striatal DAT occupancy at recreational IV doses (0.3-0.6 mg/kg); time course of striatal cocaine parallels subjective high

off_targets.clinical_consequence: QT prolongation at supratherapeutic plasma cocaine; the cocaethylene metabolite blocks hERG comparably (IC50 1.2-4.0 µM vs cocaine ~4.4 µM)
Use-dependent Na block; QRS widening, arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death; treatment of cocaine wide-QRS is sodium bicarbonate

demographic_differences.sex: Women: AUC ~40% higher in luteal vs follicular phase (smoked route); no large differences in men vs women at matched dose (doi:10.1038/sj.npp.1395344)
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: BChE deficiency (atypical pseudocholinesterase) markedly prolongs half-life and increases toxicity risk

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative biased signalling data (DAT is not a GPCR)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Identical molecular pharmacology to cocaine HCl. Only the route (smoked, free-base vaporises ~98°C vs salt decomposes ~195°C) changes kinetics.

Cocaine-like fast-binding DAT inhibitor; NET inhibition in PFC drives prefrontal DA increase (since PFC DA clearance is NET-dominated). Dexmethylphenidate (d-threo) is the eutomer ~10x more potent than l-threo.

neuroimaging.finding: Oral methylphenidate at clinical maintenance doses (0.35-0.55 mg/kg) occupies 70-80% of thalamic NET (ED50 0.14 mg/kg); striatal DAT occupancy at the same doses exceeds 50% (ED50 0.25 mg/kg; 72% at a 40 mg oral dose)

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CES1 G143E (rs71647871) carriers have 2-7x higher MPH AUC; CES1 SNPs explain ~15-30% of interindividual PK variation.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Limited downregulation at therapeutic doses; recreational IV dosing produces cocaine-like tolerance over weeks
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild dysphoria, fatigue, sleep rebound on discontinuation; no severe physical withdrawal

demographic_differences.age: Children clear MPH faster per kg than adults; CES1 expression increases through childhood
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment minor effect (CES1 expression preserved in mild cirrhosis)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as racemic MPH but with cleaner stimulant profile (l-enantiomer largely inert at CNS targets but contributes to PK variability and some peripheral NE effects).

name: Ethylphenidate

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: More DAT-selective than MPH; weaker NE-driven cardiovascular effects. Endogenous metabolite of MPH+ethanol co-use.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK studies; oral/IN/IV dosing data are anecdotal.

name: 3,4-ctmp

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Long-duration DAT inhibitor; slower onset due to lipophilicity reduces immediate reinforcement but enables strong discriminative effects.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK; clinical case reports only.

name: 4F-MPH

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Para-fluoro substitution increases potency and lipophilicity; threo diastereomer carries activity, erythro essentially inert.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK studies.

name: 4-fluoroethylphenidate

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Expected DAT-selective profile analogous to ethylphenidate with the 4-fluoro affinity boost; no direct binding data published.

data_gaps_remaining: No published binding data, no human PK.

name: 4-methylmethylphenidate
data_gaps_remaining: No published Ki/IC50 in mammalian tissue; clinical case reports only.

name: Isopropylphenidate

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: DAT-selective; resists ester hydrolysis better than MPH → longer duration. Reduced NE component lessens cardiovascular liability.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK.

name: Propylphenidate

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Propyl ester homolog; DAT-selective with affinity similar to ethylphenidate; longer half-life from slower esterase hydrolysis.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative human binding data; SAR-only inference.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Inactive metabolite of modafinil and adrafinil; does not contribute to wakefulness. No detectable DAT binding at relevant concentrations.
Inactive at DAT; does not promote wakefulness. Has shown anticonvulsant activity in animal models (mechanism unclear).

name: Adrafinil

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Itself inactive at DAT; converted hepatically into modafinil and modafinilic acid. Therapeutic effects entirely via modafinil.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Mild reversible LFT elevation with chronic use; reason French market withdrawal 2011

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative bioconversion rates in humans.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Atypical DAT inhibitor — slower binding kinetics than cocaine; preserves outward-occluded DAT conformation. Activates orexin/hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus and downstream histaminergic neurons in TMN — wakefulness is orexin/histamine dependent.

neuroimaging.finding: 39-54% striatal DAT occupancy at therapeutic doses

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduced contraceptive efficacy — modafinil 400 mg/day decreases EE AUC by ~18%

name: Bisfluoromodafinil

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Atypical DAT inhibitor — increases NAc dopamine 150-200% over baseline but without cocaine-like reinforcement. Does NOT induce CYP enzymes (unlike modafinil).

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK; no clinical trials beyond early phase.

name: CRL-40,941

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Prodrug-like — hydroxamic acid analogue of fladrafinil. Animal data (Lafon patent CA1192222A) show sedation→excitation biphasic pattern at 64-256 mg/kg in mice.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Hepatotoxicity risk inferred from adrafinil class; no human data

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK; no quantitative binding data outside patent.

name: Hydrafinil

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Proposed weak DAT inhibition + histaminergic activation; mechanism poorly characterized. Marketed as nootropic with limited preclinical evidence.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative binding data; no human PK; mechanism speculative.

name: WIN-35428

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Cocaine-like fast-binding DAT inhibitor; widely used as the canonical [3H] or [11C] DAT radioligand for in vitro autoradiography and in vivo PET.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK or subjective effect data.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Long-acting DAT/SERT inhibitor; clinically used as [123I] β-CIT SPECT tracer (DaTscan-class) for nigrostriatal degeneration imaging in Parkinson's disease.

name: RTI-113

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Highly DAT-selective phenyltropane; long-lasting discriminative effects (~5x duration of cocaine) consistent with slower DAT dissociation kinetics. Proposed agonist substitution therapy for cocaine dependence.

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: RTI-150

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Fast-acting cocaine-like DAT inhibitor; supports full self-administration in monkeys (high abuse liability).

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: RTI-133

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: N-nor (demethylated) analog of RTI-150 series; DAT-selective with similar potency to N-methyl parent.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific Ki values not in primary literature accessed.

name: Tropoxane

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Tropane-class DAT inhibitor; very limited primary literature beyond patents.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative binding/PK data publicly available.

name: Pfbt

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Lacks the C2 carbomethoxy of cocaine — much weaker DAT inhibitor (~30% potency of cocaine) but retains local anaesthetic activity at sodium channels.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative human Ki; no human PK.

name: JJC8-088

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Despite being a modafinil-derived 'atypical' template, JJC8-088 stabilises DAT in an outward-facing open conformation (cocaine-like) — produces cocaine-like reinforcement, self-administration, and reinstatement in primates. Its analog JJC8-091 (different N-substituent) favors occluded conformation and is non-reinforcing, illustrating the activity cliff in modafinil-based DAT inhibitors.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: IC50 0.13 µM at hERG — would prohibit clinical development without medchem reduction of this liability

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK or subjective effect data.

name: AHN 1-055

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Benztropine analog with slow onset; substitutes for cocaine in drug discrimination only after 90-min delay (vs minutes for cocaine), consistent with slow-binding atypical kinetics. Decreases cocaine self-administration.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK; SAR data primarily in rats/monkeys.

name: JHW-007

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Atypical DAT inhibitor — blocks cocaine-induced reward, locomotor stimulation, and sensitization without producing those effects itself. Sigma receptor antagonism may contribute to its anti-cocaine effects. Slow onset and high lipophilicity.

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: Amfonelic acid

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Structurally unrelated to cocaine/MPH; naphthyridine derived from nalidixic acid. Pure DA-selective inhibitor; protects against methamphetamine-induced striatal DA depletion if given within 8 h post-MA.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK or modern receptor-panel data.

name: CE-123

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Atypical DAT inhibitor — non-substrate, non-releasing; interacts with outward-facing DAT but stabilises a more inward-occluded state than cocaine. Reverses tetrabenazine-induced motivational deficits in rats.

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: LR-1111

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: GBR-class diphenylmethylpiperazine; ring-expanded to homopiperazine yields one of the most DAT-selective compounds known.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific numerical Ki not in primary source accessed.

name: LR-5182

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Fencamfamine-related stimulant; one stereoisomer is DA/NE-selective (NDRI), the other adds SERT activity (SNDRI). Developed by Eli Lilly in the 1970s, never marketed.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative Ki in accessible literature.

name: SoRI-20041

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Atypical allosteric DAT modulator — affects substrate uptake without affecting efflux (distinct from amphetamines and cocaine). Reduces amphetamine-induced DA release.

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: Indriline
data_gaps_remaining: Compound name not found in primary literature; possibly a misspelling of 'indatraline' or obscure designer compound. No DAT/NET/SERT Ki, PK, or mechanism data identified.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Weak parent + active hydroxybupropion metabolite (NET-selective) drives clinical NE/DA enhancement. Nicotinic antagonism is mechanistically separate and drives smoking cessation.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: competitive CYP2D6 inhibition by the reductive metabolites erythrohydrobupropion (Ki 1.7 uM) and threohydrobupropion (Ki 5.4 uM), not by hydroxybupropion or bupropion itself
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: 5-fold increase in desipramine AUC; bupropion is clinically a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2B6*6 and *18 reduce hydroxybupropion formation by ~33% without altering parent or other metabolites — implications for smoking cessation efficacy.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: No physical withdrawal; dose tapering recommended to avoid rebound depression

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Dose-dependent seizure risk — 0.4% at ≤450 mg/day; markedly higher in eating-disorder patients, bulimia, or with concurrent stimulants

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: 35% reduction in CL; reduced doses recommended
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Severe hepatic impairment: doses ≤150 mg every other day

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Selective NRI; in PFC, NET co-transports both NE and DA — atomoxetine therefore raises PFC DA despite no direct DAT activity. No striatal DA spike → no abuse liability, no reinforcement.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Convert EM to PM-like phenotype: AUC ~6-8x increase

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: PM (~7% Caucasians, <1% Asians) → 10x AUC, 5x Cmax, t1/2 21.6 h. Slow titration recommended; max 80 mg/day. UMs: lower exposure, may need higher doses.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: No physical withdrawal; non-stimulant ADHD med

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Modest QT prolongation in PMs at high exposures; FDA label warns

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Moderate hepatic impairment: 50% dose reduction; severe: 75% reduction

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Viloxazine SERTM = Serotonin and Norepinephrine Modulating Agent — at clinical Cmax occupies ~95% NET, >80% 5-HT2C/2B, 65% 5-HT7. Serotonergic component differentiates it from atomoxetine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: PMs: Cmax +21%, AUC +26% — modest; no dose adjustment required

name: Mazindol

binding.tissue_or_cell: cloned human dopamine transporter (transfected cell membranes)
cloned human norepinephrine transporter (transfected cell membranes)

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Dual NDRI + OX2R partial agonism — combines transporter blockade with orexin pathway activation (similar wakefulness mechanism to modafinil).

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative human PK studies are old/sparse.

name: Homomazindol

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Six-membered ring homologue of mazindol; SAR shows ~10x DAT affinity gain.

data_gaps_remaining: No published quantitative Ki, no human PK.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Inactive parent prodrug — hydrolysed by red blood cell aminopeptidases to d-amphetamine + L-lysine. All CNS effects via d-amphetamine. RBC hydrolysis is rate-limiting → flatter PK profile vs IR amphetamine; no escalating exposure with insufflation or IV use (cannot bypass enzymatic activation).

Inactive prodrug — quaternary pyridinium carbamate of dexmethylphenidate. Cleaved gradually in lower GI tract (small intestine/colon) to release d-MPH → delayed absorption, prolonged plasma profile. Active component is identical to Focalin.
Classic NE/DA releasing agent — substrate-type (enters via DAT/NET, displaces vesicular monoamines via VMAT2 inhibition or weak base trapping).
3-Fluoro analog of phenmetrazine; NE/DA releaser with slightly enhanced potency. Functions via DAT/NET substrate mechanism.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Case reports of AKI and critical limb ischemia in users (PMC5694401)

name: 3-Chlorophenmetrazine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: 3-Chloro analog — more potent DA releaser than 3-FPM, with measurable but modest serotonergic component.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK.

name: 4-Methylphenmetrazine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Non-selective monoamine releaser with significant 5-HT release → entactogenic profile more similar to MDMA than to phenmetrazine.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK.

name: 3,4-Methylenedioxyphenmetrazine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Despite carrying MDMA-like 3,4-methylenedioxy substitution, MDPM does NOT show robust 5-HT release — likely DAT/NET-preferring substrate-type releaser. Detected as MDMA synthesis impurity.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative DAT/NET EC50 not yet published (early notification 2024).

name: Isophenmetrazine
data_gaps_remaining: No primary pharmacology data accessible.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acts as prodrug — slow CYP N-demethylation to phenmetrazine. Resulting steady phenmetrazine plasma levels avoid the peak-trough abuse-amplifying pattern of phenmetrazine itself.

name: Brasofensine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Triple reuptake inhibitor (SNDRI) — phenyltropane scaffold. Investigated for Parkinson's disease (akinesia reversal in MPTP marmosets without dyskinesia) and major depression. Discontinued 2001.

data_gaps_remaining: Limited published human PK from terminated trials.

name: Indatraline

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Slow-onset, long-duration cocaine-like profile — blocks effects of cocaine, methamphetamine, and MDMA in animal models. Proposed as agonist substitution therapy for stimulant use disorder.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK published.

name: Tametraline

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Parent of sertraline series — potent NE/DA reuptake inhibitor (NDRI) at parent scaffold; adding 3,4-dichloro substitution + stereoisomer flip → sertraline (SSRI). Never marketed.

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative Ki not in accessible primary literature.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Sustained-release DNRI/SNDRI; extraordinarily long half-life (47-77 h) → flat PK profile, gradual onset → low abuse liability. Trials for ADHD and binge-eating disorder met endpoints, but Sumitomo abandoned 2020.

name: JNJ-7925476

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Potent SERT > DAT > NET inhibitor. Dose-dependent rise in cortical 5-HT, DA, NE in microdialysis. Antidepressant-like ED50 0.3 mg/kg in mouse TST.

data_gaps_remaining: No human data.

name: Pridefine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Noncompetitive triple reuptake inhibitor; differentiates pridefine from competitive uptake blockers. Antidepressant trials 1970s-80s; not marketed.

data_gaps_remaining: Specific Ki values not extracted from 1981 papers.

name: Indanorex

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: NDRI anorectic; also has anti-hypoglycemic activity. Discontinued.

data_gaps_remaining: No quantitative Ki in accessible primary literature.

class_name: Dopamine transporter (DAT) inhibitors — cocaine-like / phenidate-like / NDRI
shared_mechanism: Block reuptake of DA (+/- NE +/- 5-HT) at the orthosteric site of SLC6A3 (DAT). The functional split that matters clinically is binding kinetics and DAT conformation, not chemical scaffold: 'cocaine-like' inhibitors (cocaine, methylphenidate, RTI-150, WIN-35,428, JJC8-088) stabilise DAT in an outward-open conformation, exhibit fast association/dissociation, and produce euphoria; 'atypical' DAT inhibitors (modafinil, JJC8-091, JHW-007, AHN-1055, vanoxerine, CE-123) stabilise an inward-occluded conformation, exhibit slow binding/dissociation, achieve partial DAT occupancy at therapeutic doses, and lack abuse liability. NDRIs (bupropion, methylphenidate, mazindol, atomoxetine via NE→DA spillover) hit both NET and DAT; PFC dopamine clearance is NET-dominated, so NDRI gives strong cognitive enhancement without striatal DA spike — better tolerability/cardiovascular profile depends on net DAT/NET ratio.
shared_pk_summary: Cocaine: hepatic + plasma BChE + CES1 hydrolysis; t1/2 ~1 h (intranasal/IV) — fast in/out is the key abuse parameter. Methylphenidate and ester homologues: CES1 stereoselective hydrolysis (l-MPH cleared 5-10x faster than d-MPH; explains 22% vs 5% bioavailability respectively); CES1 G143E reduces clearance. Bupropion: CYP2B6→hydroxybupropion (active, NET-selective, 4-7x parent plasma); CYP2B6*6 reduces metabolite. Atomoxetine: CYP2D6 — PMs have 10x AUC, 5x Cmax, t1/2 21.6h vs 5.2h EM. Modafinil: hepatic amidase + CYP3A4/5; long t1/2 ~15h; weak CYP3A4 inducer (reduces oral contraceptive efficacy), weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. Lisdexamfetamine and serdexmethylphenidate: prodrugs (RBC aminopeptidases for LDX; gut hydrolysis for SDX) — rate-limited bioactivation deflates IV/IN abuse routes.
shared_safety: hERG block + Nav1.5 block → arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death (cocaine prototype; cocaethylene 4x worse). Atypical DAT inhibitors with sigma binding (JHW-007) and modafinil analogs (JJC8-088 IC50 0.13 µM at hERG) carry intrinsic hERG risk. Bupropion lowers seizure threshold (dose-dependent; 0.4% at ≤450 mg/day). All abused stimulants risk sympathomimetic crisis, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis at supratherapeutic doses. CES1 G143E and BChE deficiency are genetic risk factors for cocaine/MPH toxicity. CYP3A4 induction (modafinil/armodafinil) → oral contraceptive failure, reduced AUC of co-administered substrates (encorafenib, triazolam, ethinyl estradiol).
sar_summary: Cocaine scaffold: replacing C3 benzoyloxy with phenyl (phenyltropanes) → markedly higher DAT affinity (WIN-35,428 Kd 16 nM vs cocaine 300 nM) and slower dissociation; 4-iodo (RTI-55) adds SERT; 4-chloro phenyl ester (RTI-113) maximises DAT selectivity (1500x vs NET); N-substitution of benztropine scaffold from methyl→butyl shifts from cocaine-like (benztropine) to atypical/non-reinforcing (JHW-007, AHN-1055). Methylphenidate scaffold: ester chain length (Me→Et→iPr→Pr) shifts NET→DAT selectivity (d-MPH NET Ki 38 nM vs d-EPH NET Ki 3700 nM); 3,4-dichloro on phenyl (3,4-CTMP) gives 7-fold potency boost + esterase resistance → long duration. Modafinil scaffold: bis-4-fluoro (flmodafinil) boosts DAT affinity ~4x and abolishes CYP induction; small N-substituent changes in JJC8-088 vs -091 series produce activity cliff between cocaine-like and atypical profile (DAT conformation determined by single methyl difference). Phenylmorpholine releasers (phenmetrazine): 3-fluoro, 3-chloro maintain NE/DA releaser profile; 4-methyl or 3,4-methylenedioxy add 5-HT release → MDMA-like entactogen profile.

class_name: Phenyltropanes (RTI series, WIN-35,428) — cocaine-derived DAT-selective inhibitors
shared_mechanism: Tropane scaffold of cocaine with the C3 benzoyloxy ester replaced by a phenyl ring (no oxygen at C3-aryl junction); C2 carbomethoxy retained. Removes the metabolically labile ester bond → much longer half-life and slower brain entry than cocaine. Binds DAT orthosteric site competitively with cocaine; most phenyltropanes are cocaine-like (outward-facing conformation, fast on/off) but with longer duration of action because the ester is replaced by a non-hydrolysable bond. SAR: 4-aryl substituent dictates DAT selectivity (4-F = WIN-35,428 highest selectivity for DAT; 4-I = RTI-55 adds SERT; 4-Me = RTI-150). C2 substituent dictates duration (C2 phenyl ester = RTI-113 long-acting).
shared_pk_summary: Generally lipophilic with slow brain entry (vs cocaine) and long half-lives (hours to days); ester hydrolysis is the main clearance pathway when C2 carbomethoxy is retained, but C2 modifications (esters, amides) can produce very long elimination. Used primarily as PET/SPECT radioligands (WIN-35,428 [11C], β-CIT/RTI-55 [123I]) in human DAT imaging — slow brain kinetics is desirable for imaging but argues against therapeutic translation in pure form.
shared_safety: Phenyltropanes inherit cocaine's cardiovascular off-targets (hERG, Nav1.5) to varying degrees; specific human data sparse since most are research tools. RTI-113 and others have been tested in primate self-administration with high reinforcing efficacy, but slower onset reduces (rather than eliminates) abuse liability. Atypical phenyltropanes (those stabilising occluded DAT conformation) like indatraline have lower abuse liability.
sar_summary: C3-aryl 4-position controls selectivity: H ~ cocaine; F → DAT-selective (WIN-35,428); I → adds SERT (RTI-55); Me → cocaine-like (RTI-150); 3,4-Cl2 → high potency. C2 substituent controls duration: methyl ester (cocaine) hydrolysed by esterases (t1/2 min); phenyl ester (RTI-113) and amides resist hydrolysis (t1/2 hours). N8 substituent (methyl→nor or larger groups) modulates affinity and kinetics: nor- generally less potent; larger N-substituents can flip from cocaine-like to atypical.

class_name: Atypical DAT inhibitors — modafinil-derived (JJC, CE, SoRI series)
shared_mechanism: Diphenylmethyl-sulfinyl-acetamide scaffold (modafinil) and ring-expanded/N-substituted variants. Mechanism distinct from cocaine: at the DAT, these compounds stabilise inward-facing or occluded conformations (rather than outward-open) and exhibit SLOW association and dissociation kinetics. Slow kinetics → blunted reinforcement (the dopaminergic spike does not have sharp onset) → low abuse liability. Some (JJC8-088 specifically) violate this rule by stabilising outward-open, demonstrating the conformation hypothesis: modafinil-derived chemistry can produce both atypical and cocaine-like profiles depending on subtle N- and aryl-substituent choices (activity cliff). Modafinil parent additionally activates orexin/hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus → histamine TMN → wakefulness (DAT inhibition alone is insufficient to explain its eugeroic profile at clinical doses).
shared_pk_summary: Modafinil: oral t1/2 ~12-15h (racemate); armodafinil 10-15h; bioavailability high (~80%); CYP3A4/5 + amidase metabolism to inactive sulfone (t1/2 40h) and acid (t1/2 7h). Modafinil is weak CYP3A4 inducer and weak CYP2C19 inhibitor; flmodafinil is reportedly NOT a CYP inducer (key advantage). Adrafinil prodrug hepatically converted to modafinil (~50%) but carries additional hepatotoxicity from hydroxamic acid moiety. Atypical research compounds (JJC, CE-123) have very long half-lives by design to maintain slow brain kinetics.
shared_safety: Major concern: hERG block (JJC8-088 IC50 0.13 µM; medchem effort to reduce). Modafinil: rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome / DRESS (FDA label warns), CYP3A4 induction → contraceptive failure. Vanoxerine: multi-channel cardiac block (hERG IC50 0.84 nM, Nav1.5, Cav1.2) but minimal APD prolongation — paradoxically antiarrhythmic. Atypical DAT profile generally low abuse liability — proposed mechanism for stimulant use disorder treatment.
sar_summary: Single N-substituent change (e.g. JJC8-088 vs -091) flips conformational preference and abuse-likability: this is the 'activity cliff'. Adding fluorines to diphenyl rings (flmodafinil vs modafinil) increases DAT affinity ~4x without changing atypical character and removes CYP induction. Hydroxamic acid moiety (adrafinil, fladrafinil) confers hepatotoxicity. CE-123 series replaces sulfinyl with thio/sulfonyl groups to tune selectivity.

class_name: Atypical DAT inhibitors — N-substituted benztropines (AHN, JHW series)
shared_mechanism: Tropane-diphenylmethylether scaffold of benztropine. Despite high DAT affinity (Ki single-digit nM), N-substituent (especially N-butyl, JHW-007) yields atypical DAT inhibitor profile: slow onset, partial DAT occupancy at high doses, no cocaine-like reinforcement, blocks (rather than substitutes for) cocaine in self-administration and discrimination. Mechanism: stabilises DAT in inward-occluded conformation. Many in this series additionally bind sigma-1 and sigma-2 receptors at therapeutic concentrations, which may contribute to anti-cocaine effects. Slow binding kinetics + DAT-independent striatal binding sites (residual binding in DAT-knockout mice) are signatures of the class.
shared_pk_summary: Highly lipophilic → slow brain entry and prolonged half-lives. Limited human PK published. Benztropine itself: oral, t1/2 ~16h; N-substituted analogues lipophilicity-dependent.
shared_safety: Inherited from benztropine: anticholinergic burden (M1, M2 muscarinic antagonism — dry mouth, urinary retention, cognitive impairment in elderly); H1 antihistamine (sedation). Sigma-1 antagonism may have unknown long-term consequences. Lower abuse liability is the chief advantage.
sar_summary: N-methyl (benztropine, AHN-1055) → modest DAT affinity, partial cocaine-like profile. N-butyl/longer (JHW-007) → atypical, non-reinforcing, cocaine-antagonist profile. Bis-(4-fluoro) on diphenyl improves DAT selectivity. Removing tropane methyl yields nor-analogues with altered conformational preference at DAT.

class_name: Phenylmorpholine substrate-type monoamine releasers (phenmetrazine and analogues)
shared_mechanism: Substituted phenylmorpholine scaffold. Acts as substrate at DAT and NET — taken up via transporter, then displaces vesicular monoamines (via VMAT2 substrate competition / weak-base trapping) → reverse transport of DA and NE into synapse (efflux). Distinct from cocaine-class uptake blockers — releaser pharmacology produces stronger and more sustained DA/NE rise. Aryl-ring substitution dictates serotonergic add-on: parent phenmetrazine essentially NE/DA-selective (negligible SERT); 4-methyl (4-MPM) and 3,4-methylenedioxy (MDPM) shift toward 5-HT releaser activity (MDMA-like entactogen profile).
shared_pk_summary: Phenmetrazine: oral t1/2 ~8h. Phendimetrazine (N-methyl analogue): inactive prodrug, slow CYP N-demethylation to phenmetrazine — flatter PK profile reduces abuse liability vs phenmetrazine itself. Fluorinated analogues (3-FPM) and Cl-substituted (3-CPM) have variable PK; halogenation typically extends duration via metabolic stabilisation.
shared_safety: Releaser pharmacology produces stronger sympathomimetic load than uptake-blocker class — hypertension, tachycardia, vasoconstriction (3-FPM AKI + critical limb ischemia case reports). MDMA-like analogues (4-MPM) add serotonin syndrome risk and 5-HT2B-mediated valvulopathy concern with chronic use.
sar_summary: Halogen at C3 (F, Cl) maintains NE/DA selectivity and modestly potentiates DAT release. Halogen at C4 (4-F) similar. C4 methyl or 3,4-methylenedioxy adds substantial SERT releaser activity → MDMA-like profile. N-methylation (phendimetrazine) abolishes activity, generating slow-release prodrug of demethylated form (phenmetrazine).

class_name: Eugeroic afinils (modafinil, adrafinil, fladrafinil, hydrafinil, etc.)
shared_mechanism: Predominant clinically active member is modafinil. Mechanism is multimodal: (1) weak DAT inhibition (modafinil DAT Ki ~4 µM; PET shows 50% striatal DAT occupancy at 200-400 mg in humans), (2) ORE EXIN/hypocretin neuron activation in lateral hypothalamus (modafinil increases orexin neuron c-Fos), (3) downstream histaminergic TMN activation (modafinil-induced wakefulness requires intact histamine neurons), (4) modest glutamate↑ and GABA↓ in cortical networks. Adrafinil is hepatic prodrug of modafinil; fladrafinil is bis-fluoro adrafinil; flmodafinil/bisfluoromodafinil is bis-fluoro modafinil (improved DAT affinity, no CYP induction); hydrafinil is structurally unrelated fluorenol with weak/poorly characterised mechanism.
shared_pk_summary: Modafinil: oral F ~80%, t1/2 12-15h, Tmax 2h, protein binding 60%. Metabolised CYP3A4/5 + hepatic amidase to inactive sulfone (t1/2 40h) and acid (t1/2 7h). Weak CYP3A4 inducer (clinically relevant for hormonal contraceptives, triazolam, encorafenib), weak CYP2C19 inhibitor (warfarin, omeprazole). Armodafinil (R-enantiomer): t1/2 ~15h (slightly longer than racemate because R-eutomer clears slower than S). Adrafinil: prodrug t1/2 ~1h before conversion to modafinil; adds hepatotoxicity (LFT elevation; French market withdrawal 2011).
shared_safety: Rare Stevens-Johnson syndrome, DRESS, toxic epidermal necrolysis (FDA boxed-warning class). CYP3A4 induction → contraceptive failure. Adrafinil/fladrafinil class hepatotoxicity (hydroxamic acid moiety). Generally low abuse liability — but reinforcing in vulnerable populations; classified US Schedule IV.
sar_summary: Bis-4-fluoro on diphenyl (flmodafinil, fladrafinil) increases DAT affinity ~4x and removes CYP3A4 induction. Hydroxamic acid (adrafinil, fladrafinil) → hepatotoxicity. Sulfinyl→sulfonyl (modafinil sulfone): inactive. Acetamide→acetic acid (modafinil acid): inactive. R-enantiomer of modafinil is the eutomer (slower clearance, similar potency).

shared_mechanism: Block NET (SLC6A2) with high selectivity over DAT and SERT. In prefrontal cortex, NET co-transports BOTH NE and DA (because PFC has low DAT density), so selective NET inhibition raises PFC DA without striatal DA spike → cognitive enhancement without abuse liability. No reinforcement, no euphoria. Viloxazine adds serotonergic activity (5-HT2C partial agonism, 5-HT2B/2C/7 antagonism) — differentiates from atomoxetine. Both used in ADHD as non-stimulant alternatives.
shared_pk_summary: Atomoxetine: oral F 63% (EM) / 94% (CYP2D6 PM); t1/2 5.2h EM / 21.6h PM (10x AUC, 5x Cmax); protein binding 98% (albumin). CYP2D6 primary; CYP2C19 minor. Viloxazine ER: t1/2 7h, Tmax 5h, protein binding 76%; UGT1A9/UGT2B15 primary; CYP2D6 minor (PMs have only 21-26% increase, no dose adjust). Viloxazine is strong CYP1A2 inhibitor (caffeine, theophylline AUC doubled).
shared_safety: Atomoxetine: rare hepatic injury (boxed warning), modest QT prolongation in PMs, suicidality concern (FDA boxed warning, pediatric). Viloxazine: CYP1A2 interactions (caffeine, theophylline, melatonin, clozapine). Both: dry mouth, decreased appetite, insomnia common; no significant abuse liability.
sar_summary: Phenoxypropylamine (atomoxetine) and morpholine (viloxazine) scaffolds. CYP2D6 stereoselective metabolism (atomoxetine R-isomer hydroxylated faster than S). NET selectivity over DAT/SERT 290-fold (atomoxetine) to 100-fold (viloxazine) — high enough to avoid abuse.

class_name: Serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitors (SNDRIs / triple reuptake inhibitors)
shared_mechanism: Simultaneous inhibition of SERT, NET, and DAT at the orthosteric sites. Designed for major depression with the theory that DA component would address anhedonia/motivation deficit unmet by SSRIs/SNRIs. Most programs failed because hitting DAT at antidepressant doses creates abuse liability (e.g., dasotraline) or hERG/cardiovascular issues. Dasotraline succeeded by extreme PK flattening (t1/2 47-77h → infusion-like exposure, no peak-trough abuse pattern) but was discontinued for commercial reasons. Indatraline and brasofensine are classic research-grade SNDRIs.
shared_pk_summary: Variable; medicinal-chemistry effort focused on extending half-life to avoid peak abuse liability. Dasotraline t1/2 47-77h; brasofensine and indatraline shorter. Most metabolised by hepatic CYPs.
shared_safety: DAT activity drives abuse liability if PK is sharp. Pridefine: noncompetitive uptake inhibition mode (mechanistic curiosity). Hypertension/tachycardia from NE + DA effects. Serotonin syndrome risk if combined with SSRIs/MAOIs. Hepatic concerns with several compounds.
sar_summary: Phenyltropane (brasofensine), aminoindane (indatraline, dasotraline), pyrroloisoquinoline (JNJ-7925476), pyrrolidine (pridefine). Within each scaffold, halogen substitution on aryl moiety tunes SERT vs DAT vs NET potency ratios. Dasotraline (1R,4S-aminotetralin) directly derived from tametraline → sertraline series with stereochemistry tuned for SNDRI rather than SSRI profile.
